articles.title: LeBron James teases partnership with Polymarket
articles.description: LeBron James on Saturday teased an upcoming partnership with the prediction markets platform Polymarket in a social media post.

articles.title: Putin begins talks with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner on ending war with Ukraine
articles.description: Moscow and Kyiv vow not to strike each other’s capitals for three days during negotiations Russian president Vladimir Putin began talks with US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on ending more than four years of war in Ukraine in the Kremlin Saturday, ahead of their first visit to Kyiv expected on Sunday. Both Russia and Ukraine vowed not to strike each other’s capitals for three days during the negotiations, as Washington tries to revive US-led talks to end Europe’s worst conflict since the second world war.

articles.title: Robin Morgan, child star who became feminist, poet and editor, dies aged 85
articles.description: Leading second-wave feminist co-founded Women’s Media Center with Jane Fonda and Gloria Steinem Robin Morgan, a child star of the 1940s and 50s who grew up to become an all-American radical as a poet, essayist, editor and second-wave feminist, has died. She was 85. Morgan’s death was confirmed Saturday by the Women’s Media Center, an organization she co-founded with Jane Fonda and the celebrated author and activist Gloria Steinem , who died Wednesday.

articles.title: London Paddington fire causes rail chaos as Heathrow trains cancelled
articles.description: Blaze causes electricity supply failure and disruption of services to airport and Reading A fire near a train track in the London Paddington area has caused major disruption, with services to Heathrow airport cancelled. The fire caused an electricity supply failure which has left all lines between Paddington and the airport blocked, National Rail said.

articles.title: Egyptian TV presenter among 12 sentenced to death for drug crime
articles.description: Sarah Khalifa, 39, charged with forming organised criminal gang to manufacture and traffick drugs An Egyptian court sentenced a well-known television presenter and 11 others to death for manufacturing and trafficking narcotics in a sprawling drug case, official media reported on Saturday. The presenter, Sarah Khalifa, 39, is best known for her programme Mission Impossible, which dealt with issues concerning security and crime.

articles.title: Farage brushes aside Reform controversies in closing conference speech – UK politics as it happened
articles.description: ‘Sometimes we will get things wrong and get a bit of a kicking for it,’ party leader tells gathering in Birmingham No real mention by Anderson of the problems that overshadowed events yesterday. He ended his opening speech saying: "Yesterday was great. Today is going to be absolutely brilliant.” Laila Cunningham is speaking next.

articles.title: ‘I wasn’t even listening,’ Farage says of donations scandal meeting
articles.description: Reform UK leader maintains innocence in overseas funding controversy on last day of party conference UK politics live Nigel Farage has claimed that he “wasn’t even listening” during a meeting at the centre of a controversy about whether his party considered evading the law on accepting donations from overseas. The Reform UK leader also claimed he knew donation law “better than anybody” during interviews as he sought to salvage the final day of his party conference from the fallout that has already cost him two of his closest aides.

articles.title: Black-clad protesters in balaclavas block road at port of Dover in Kent
articles.description: Port authorities say access roads ‘free flowing’ again after large group forces road closures in both directions Dozens of people dressed in black and wearing balaclavas blocked the road at the port of Dover in Kent, forcing closures in both directions on Saturday morning. Kent police said they were were in attendance and engaging with the protest, which the Port of Dover described as a “public order incident”. No arrests were made during the incident. Responsibility for the demonstration appears to have been claimed by an anti-immigration group with links to the far right.

articles.title: U.S. attacks 3 Iranian oil tankers after missiles target Navy warships
articles.description: Three Iranian crude oil carriers were hit by U.S. forces on Saturday near Iran's key oil export hub, Kharg Island, in the Gulf, U.S. Central Command reported.

articles.title: US military says it struck three Iranian tankers after American warships came under missile attack
articles.description: Officials said US aircraft carrier and destroyer avoided attacks before three Iranian tankers were struck by the US The US military said Saturday it struck three Iranian oil tankers after US navy warships came under missile attack, further escalating tensions in the region and warning it would “if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet”. According to the military, a US aircraft carrier and destroyer avoided “multiple unprovoked Iranian attacks” while patrolling the region. No US personnel were injured.

articles.title: Trump’s state capitalism comes to the oil industry with his unprecedented Venezuela deal
articles.description: The deal comes eight months after Washington ousted former President Nicolás Maduro in a military raid.

articles.title: Raise the Colours leader given access to Reform UK conference while on bail
articles.description: Ryan Bridge, arrested this year on suspicion of religiously and racially aggravated harassment, says party invited him The leader of a flag campaign group who was arrested on suspicion of causing religiously and racially aggravated harassment was given access to Reform UK’s annual conference. Ryan Bridge, whose Raise the Colours group has put up hundreds of union and St George flags across England, told the Guardian he was invited to the conference.

articles.title: Cut the cameras: Flock surveillance cameras spur rare bipartisan backlash
articles.description: Politicians on the right and left are pushing back against Flock as more Americans voice opposition to the tech Growing factions from both sides of the political aisle in the US are pushing back against surveillance cameras made by a single company, a rare response in a sharply divided country with a president pushing an unwaveringly pro-tech agenda. The bipartisan backlash against Flock Safety cameras resembles nationwide rage toward the construction of large datacenters that power artificial intelligence. Polling shows roughly 75% of Americans oppose new datacenter construction in their areas.

articles.title: Civilians among at least 60 killed in Yemen as ground fighting escalates
articles.description: Houthi rebel offensive against government forces on west coast leads to some of deadliest clashes in years Clashes between Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces and the Iran-aligned Houthi rebel movement have killed more than 60 people, including civilians, as the Houthis pushed forward with a military offensive on Yemen’s western coast. Twenty-six government troops and 31 Houthi fighters were killed during several hours of fighting in the country’s south-west on Saturday, medical and military sources told Agence France-Presse (AFP). A missile strike also killed six civilians and injured seven others travelling by bus in the city of Taiz.

articles.title: Abel: Two ways Berkshire hopes to cash in on AI
articles.description: Berkshire Hathaway CEO Greg Abel tells CNBC the company is pursuing AI opportunities on two paths.

articles.title: This enhanced geothermal project aims to unlock gigawatts of power to fuel the data center boom
articles.description: Power demand in the U.S. is rising. Fervo Energy bets that its project in Utah will prove that enhanced geothermal can be part of the power mix going forward.

articles.title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial ends in dramatic deadlock – what comes next?
articles.description: District attorney must decide whether to retry case after jury’s failure to reach verdict despite hours of deliberation Lindsay Clancy, prosecutors, defense lawyers, the judge and millions watching on are back where they started after her five-week trial over the murder of her three children ended in a mistrial. America’s saddest case has ceased for the moment, but the legal wrangling is not over, and a second trial could now be on the horizon, prolonging and repeating an agonizing spectacle that has gripped America and the world.

articles.title: GM vs. Ford: U.S. defense, energy sectors add to automakers' century-old rivalry
articles.description: General Motors and Ford are looking for new potential growth areas, including by seeking military contracts and getting into energy storage businesses.

articles.title: Meet the CISO: A new front line star in the AI cybersecurity war

articles.title: Rescuers in Nepal find two more people alive after flash flood disaster
articles.description: Chinese man at Trishuli hydropower project and Nepali woman in Nuwakot found 10 days into rescue operation Emergency responders have rescued a Chinese man and a Nepali woman in two separate operations as authorities continued to search for thousands of people missing 10 days after massive floods hit Nepal. The Nepali military said on Saturday a joint team comprising personnel from its army and South Korean disaster experts rescued the man from a 225-metre (740ft) tunnel in the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower project, and that he was undergoing a health assessment. Pictures showed him being evacuated by helicopter after being carried out of the tunnel.

articles.title: ‘Guilt by association’: why seven international aid workers were killed in Israeli airstrike
articles.description: Exclusive: Guardian investigation reveals targeting of World Central Kitchen convoy was result of widely used military tactic Death on the road to Rafah: the night the IDF targeted WCK aid workers Seven aid workers killed in an airstrike in Gaza were marked as targets under an Israeli military practice of establishing guilt by association, a Guardian investigation shows. A top Israeli military prosecutor announced last month that he would not pursue criminal proceedings for the April 2024 incident in which drones fired missiles at three clearly marked World Central Kitchen (WCK) cars soon after they had escorted a food aid delivery to Gaza. Three British humanitarian workers along with an Australian, a Palestinian, a Pole and a dual US-Canadian national were killed.

articles.title: First professional St Nick with Down’s syndrome inducted into International Santa Claus Hall of Fame
articles.description: Atlanta’s Bradley Carlisle first played Kris Kringle for kids with Down’s syndrome and has now completed elite Santa Academy After recently gaining recognition as the first professional Santa Claus with Down’s syndrome in the US, Bradley Carlisle has already gotten a lot more than the traditional serving of milk and cookies that is usually left out for Father Christmas each year. That is because the 37-year-old community theater actor from suburban Atlanta landed an honorary induction into the International Santa Claus Hall of Fame upon completing one of the largest Christmas performer schools in the US in late August – a distinction meant to recognize the important representation his emergence on the holiday scene has brought, according to his supporters.

articles.title: Europe would not be able to sustain war of attrition with Russia, defence officials say
articles.description: Security experts fear Putin may be winning hybrid war with the west amid rise of pro-Kremlin, far-right parties Defence planners working with Nato fear that if war broke out with Russia, Europe could not currently sustain a prolonged war of attrition owing to a public lack of war readiness, a conference on the future of European military coordination heard this week. The pessimism reflects concern that Russia may be winning a so-called hybrid war with Europe, weakening the options available to Nato war planners in the event of military conflict.

articles.title: Captain calamity: Pete Hegseth under fire for ‘inept’ leadership of US military
articles.description: The US defense secretary faces internal dissent and discord at the Pentagon, accused of focusing on culture war issues and his own political ambitions as the Iran war drags on In a different Washington, under a different president, a return to the well-worn playbook of all-out sanctions to counter Iran might have been the signal for a publicity-hungry US secretary of defense to adopt a lower profile. But these are no ordinary times. And Pete Hegseth is no ordinary defense secretary.

articles.title: ‘It cost me many friendships’: former Brazil military chief reveals inside struggle to stop Bolsonaro’s coup
articles.description: Carlos de Almeida Baptista Júnior describes 2022 meeting in new book as ex-leader’s son vies with Lula for presidency The far-right populist Jair Bolsonaro was in his final days as Brazil’s president when, six weeks after losing the election and still refusing to recognise the result, he summoned the heads of the armed forces to a meeting. The defence minister, Gen Paulo Sérgio Nogueira de Oliveira, took out a document from a plastic folder and handed copies to the commanders of the navy, army and air force.

articles.title: Gaza refugee says sister-in-law ‘would be alive’ if Home Office had let her come to UK
articles.description: Anwar, who lives in Glasgow, says Home Office refused visa application despite Maryam having cancer A man living in the UK has said he believes his sister-in-law who died from cancer in Gaza would still be alive today if the Home Office had agreed to bring her and her family to Britain. Anwar, who lives in Glasgow, fled Gaza in 2020 and was granted refugee status in the UK in 2021. After the destruction of large areas of Gaza by Israeli forces following the Hamas attacks on Israel in October 2023, he applied to bring his brother Hassan, Hassan’s wife, Maryam , their two young children and other family members to the UK in October 2025. He said the Home Office rejected their application.

articles.title: Sweden confirms 458 Britons deported or forcibly removed since Brexit
articles.description: Scale of deportations made public for first time amid criticism of hardline approach to UK citizens Sweden has confirmed 458 British citizens have been deported or forcibly removed by police since Brexit. It is the first time the scale of the deportations of citizens who failed to secure residency in Sweden post-Brexit has been made public and comes amid mounting criticism of a cruel and hardline approach to Britons who had chosen to make the country their home before Brexit.

articles.title: Sydney reaches 33C in potentially warmest start to spring since mid-1800s, while snow forecast in southern NSW
articles.description: A total fire ban is in place for greater Sydney with extreme fire danger exacerbated by hot and windy conditions Maximum temperatures in Sydney during the first days of September were on track to match the city’s midsummer average of 26.4C, warmer than any other start to spring since the city’s Observatory Hill station opened in 1858.

articles.title: ‘Every girl now wants to be a boxer’: excitement in Katie Taylor’s home town for her valedictory bout
articles.description: Irish boxer lauded for her tenacity and inspiration before her last fight in front of 80,000 people at Croke Park When Katie Taylor steps into the ring on Saturday night to defend her titles and once again enthral Ireland, there will be a bittersweet tinge. After a singular career that pioneered women’s boxing, the super-lightweight champion and Olympic gold medallist is bowing out. She is 40 and it is to be her final bout. “The end of an era, isn’t it?” said Trevor McMahon, her brother-in-law and founder of a gym where she trains. “It’ll be an amazing night but it’ll also be a little bit sad. Everything she did, it might not ever be achieved again.”

articles.title: Death on the road to Rafah: the night the IDF targeted World Central Kitchen aid workers
articles.description: The Israeli army had helped plan the delivery of food aid on 1 April 2024, but things went wrong from the beginning and ended in seven deaths • Exclusive: why seven international aid workers were killed in Israeli airstrike On the evening of 1 April 2024, a team of aid workers from World Central Kitchen (WCK) stood on Gaza’s Mediterranean shore overseeing the unloading of a barge full of desperately needed food on a makeshift jetty made of sand and rubble. The Gaza war had been raging for six months and Israel’s closure of land crossings had left the whole territory facing the threat of famine. WCK and local Palestinian contractors had constructed the jetty out of everything they could lay their hands on, including debris from the bombed house of one of the contractors, so that the pallets of humanitarian assistance could be delivered by boat from Cyprus.

articles.title: Trump’s ‘retribution’ could now include Falklands as favor to Milei – and revenge on the UK
articles.description: US president suggests he might support his Argentinian acolyte’s drive to reclaim sovereignty of disputed islands Donald Trump has long embraced vengeance. “I am your retribution,” he declared to an admiring audience at the 2023 Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) as he commenced his march back to the White House. It is unlikely Argentina, and far-flung holdovers of the former British empire, were on the US president’s mind at the time.

articles.title: UN votes to adopt new world map that shows Africa’s true scale
articles.description: Togo-sponsored resolution called to phase out traditional map that depicts continent as similar size to Greenland The United Nations has voted to adopt a resolution for the world to formally phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe in favour of one that more accurately displays Africa’s size. In a session at its headquarters in New York, the UN general assembly officially retired the 16th-century Mercator projection in favour of one based on the more accurate 2018 Equal Earth design.

articles.title: Colombia president provokes disgust by posing with bodies of ‘terrorists’
articles.description: Abelardo De La Espriella posts video of himself with rows of body bags as performative populism continues to sweep Americas Colombia’s hardline president, Abelardo De La Espriella, has provoked outrage after posting a video on social media in which he strides through rows of white body bags that he says contained the corpses of 23 “neutralised” guerrillas. De La Espriella took power last month vowing “all-out war” against illegal armed groups and he published the footage on Thursday in an apparent attempt to show he was fulfilling that pledge.

articles.title: Two workers pulled alive from tunnel nine days after Nepal-Tibet floods
articles.description: Officials say pair were rescued from Trishuli 3A hydropower tunnel in Nepal after being trapped at depth of 170 metres Two people have been pulled out alive from a hydropower tunnel in Nepal nine days after deadly flash floods buried the projects in deep mud and left them trapped. The workers were rescued during an operation at the Trishuli 3A tunnel, a hydropower project in one of the areas worst affected by last week’s floods , according to the army spokesperson Brig Gen Raja Ram Basnet.

articles.title: UK hits back at Argentinian Falklands claim and insists islands remain British
articles.description: Ed Miliband says Britain’s position remains ‘unwavering’ in response to remarks by Argentina’s president UK politics live – latest updates British ministers have hit back after the Argentinian president said “winds of change” favourable to his country’s claim to the Falklands were “blowing around the world”. The latest jump on Thursday lifted the yen to its highest level against the dollar in a month, at 155.57, and followed a 0.9% move the previous day.

articles.title: Spain’s PM says no evidence ‘whatsoever’ Morocco behind Ceuta border breach
articles.description: Pedro Sánchez continues to defend Rabat after police report claiming border forces helped 70,000 cross border Europe live – latest updates Spain has seen no evidence “whatsoever” that Morocco planned or facilitated a mass border breach into its north African territory of Ceuta, the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has told parliament. The address on Thursday followed the emergence of a police report, commissioned by a judge and widely quoted in the media, claiming Moroccan border forces had actively aided about 70,000 people to cross the border in late July.

articles.title: 聯合國警告可能出現「超大型」厄爾尼諾現象，各國須準備應對
articles.description: 聯合國世界氣象組織（WMO）警告，這種自然天氣現象可能為全球經濟帶來衝擊。

articles.title: Dozens of trapped hydropower tunnel workers in Nepal could still be alive, official says
articles.description: About 46 people believed to be trapped in ‘room-like’ structure inside hydro plant tunnel on Nepal-Tibet border After the flood: human suffering on an unfathomable scale in Nepal’s worst-hit districts Nepal authorities have said they are “confident” that dozens of workers in Nepal’s Rasuwagadhi hydropower plant are still alive, more than a week after deadly flash floods left them trapped in an underground chamber. Authorities said that at least 639 workers were still missing from hydropower plants built along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Triushuli rivers.

articles.title: ‘We continue to suffer’: victims of apartheid-era Sharpeville massacre demand compensation
articles.description: Claim relating to 1960 attack on hundreds of protesters part of wave of litigation over apartheid crimes in South Africa The day dawned brightly on 21 March 1960, as residents of the South African township of Sharpeville gathered to protest against pass laws, which forced “Black, Indian and Coloured” South Africans to carry documents at all times specifying where they were allowed to be. Abraham Mofokeng joined the march, one of dozens organised nationwide by the Pan Africanist Congress (PAC), a breakaway group from the African National Congress (ANC). “The weather was very nice, the sun was out. You could not have suspected that the day would go so horribly,” said Mofokeng, who was then a 20-year-old factory worker.

articles.title: 美國航母「林肯號」航行250天終抵泰國，這是我們目前知道的情況
articles.description: 美國核動力航空母艦「亞伯拉罕·林肯號」（USS Abraham Lincoln）在海上連續航行250天，現在終於抵達泰國靠岸，近5,000名船員得以休息。

articles.title: The world appears to be entering a higher-rate era. Here’s who will pay the price
articles.description: The bond sell-off is owed to a mix of high government debt issuance, an oil-price shock that has reignited inflation concerns, and expectations of higher rates.

articles.title: 莫迪敦促普京結束烏克蘭戰爭，他能勸得動嗎？
articles.description: 印度經濟高度依賴自俄羅斯進口的折扣石油。自2022年普京發動對烏克蘭的全面入侵以來，莫迪已多次向普京提出過類似的呼籲。

articles.title: 《肖申克的救贖》中國公映：官方字幕翻譯何以引發爭議？
articles.description: 例如，同性戀（homosexual）譯成「不同的人」，queer 譯成「變態」，「make love under tree」（直譯應為「在樹下做愛」）譯成「許下終身」。

articles.title: Why Hilton calls this Asian country the fastest-growing tourism market
articles.description: Hilton says one Asian country is the most exciting global tourism market as regional travel surges.

articles.title: China’s falling emissions amid Iran war spark hope of decarbonisation watershed
articles.description: Oil consumption plummets and EV sales soar as analysts say demand may not fully return even if crude price falls China’s carbon dioxide emissions fell by 1% after the outbreak of the US-Israeli war on Iran, thanks to a sharp reduction in oil consumption and a steady rise in the use of electric vehicles and public transport, analysis shows. The report reveals the role of clean energy in cushioning the price shocks caused by the strait of Hormuz crisis to the world’s biggest oil importer. It also reinforces hopes that China, which is the world’s biggest greenhouse gas emitter, may be nearing a turning point in decarbonising its economy.

articles.title: 黃之鋒：從學運領袖到國安法囚犯，重獲自由未有期
articles.description: 自2020年11月被關押以來，香港民主派活動人士黃之鋒被控多宗罪名，至今已身在獄中接近六年。

articles.title: 黃之鋒「勾結外國勢力危害國家安全」案認罪，最高可囚終身
articles.description: 現年29歲的民主派活動人士黃之鋒，在法庭上承認一項中國《香港國安法》下的「串謀勾結外國勢力危害國家安全」罪，判刑押後至另日進行。至今，黃之鋒已失去自由逾2,100天。

articles.title: 重獲自由未有期 回顧黃之鋒的公共生涯
articles.description: 香港民主派活動人士黃之鋒被控違反《香港國安法》下的「串謀勾結外國勢力」罪，2026年9月2日在高等法院出庭並認罪，法官將案件押後判刑。

articles.title: Barclays faces complaint over backing for power plant near world’s largest mangrove forest
articles.description: Bangladeshi complainants allege Rampal power station’s pollution and climate risks threaten the Sunderbans, a world heritage site Barclays Bank is facing a formal complaint over its financial links to a coal-fired power station near the Sundarbans, the world’s largest mangrove forest and home to millions of people in Bangladesh and India. Three complainants from the region have submitted a case to the UK government’s Office for Responsible Business Conduct, alleging that the British bank breached international guidelines by underwriting companies involved in the emission-heavy Maitree super thermal power project, also known as the Rampal power plant.

articles.title: New constitution in Guinea-Bissau will undermine democracy, opponents say
articles.description: Referendum result means fewer seats in parliament and new rules on candidates, ahead of December elections Guinea-Bissau voters have approved a new constitution, which critics say will undermine democracy, that significantly expands presidential powers ahead of elections due in December. According to provisional results, 70% of voters approved sweeping changes in the tiny west African state’s first constitutional amendment since revisions that ended the one-party socialist state more than three decades ago.

articles.title: 美國公司獲批委內瑞拉油田百年開採權 分析人士迷惑 國民震怒
articles.description: 委內瑞拉近期沒有舉行選舉，或者說，沒有任何明確的選舉計劃，這在許多反對者看來是一種背叛。

articles.title: Japan halves speed limit to 30km/h on all narrow city streets
articles.description: Speed limit dropped from 60km/h for around 70% of general roads in the hope of making narrow streets of crowded cities safer Drivers on residential roads in Japan have been forced to take their foot off the accelerator, after the speed limit was slashed from 60km/h (37mph) to 30km/h in an attempt to reduce deaths and injuries among pedestrians on narrow urban streets. The new limit, which went into effect on Tuesday, applies to residential roads with no centre line or maximum speed signs, media reports said.

articles.title: Relief as five Australians missing in Nepal-Tibet flood disaster found alive
articles.description: Several missing Australians have been found since Tuesday morning, bringing the total citizens unaccounted for to 38 Australians missing in the Nepal floods: what we know so far A total of five Australians missing after devastating floods ravaged the Nepal-Tibet border last week have been found. Of the five Australians confirmed safe, one was found in Nepal, one in Tibet, and three outside the crisis-hit area. The total number still missing is 38.

articles.title: 尼泊爾—西藏泥石流：堰塞湖和冰湖是下一個「定時炸彈」？
articles.description: 事發河谷上游已形成兩個堰塞湖。與此同時，原本散佈在喜馬拉雅山區的冰川湖，在災區內有10座被標記為高風險，專家形容它們是「定時炸彈」。

articles.title: 日本企業大舉押注印度　中國風險加深之際尋求新成長
articles.description: 日本企業正加碼布局印度，因國內市場萎縮及中國風險升高。

articles.title: British aid worker mistakenly identified as a survivor of Nepal-Tibet disaster
articles.description: More than 1,000 people confirmed dead and more than 4,000, including 36 British nationals, remain missing A British aid worker was mistakenly identified by Nepalese authorities as a rescued survivor after returning to Kathmandu on a humanitarian aid flight. Alastair Chambers, a 45-year-old former Gloucester councillor, said he flew to Nepal last week to distribute sleeping bags, food and essentials to communities cut off by collapsed bridges.

articles.title: 上合組織25週年：中國舞台、伊朗考驗，還是「清談場所」？
articles.description: 「整套東西說穿了，就是共識旗幟下的中國工具箱。成員加入自己感興趣的部分，沒有人被要求成為盟友。北京不要求同盟式義務，它要的是背書、參與，以及不要阻擋（中國）。」

articles.title: 泥石流摧毀西藏吉隆口岸的關鍵幾分鐘
articles.description: 吉隆口岸位處西藏與尼泊爾的重要貿易通路之上，中國與尼泊爾兩側各有數以百計外國旅客在泥石流衝擊後下落不明。

articles.title: 「大家都是做做樣子」：香港高中公民科推行五週年
articles.description: 香港高中以「公民與社會發展科」取代通識科至今已五年，學生前往中國大陸考察亦由過去的自願參與，逐步成為課程安排的一部分。2025/26學年，約有5萬名高中學生參與相關考察，政府資助逾8,400萬港元。BBC中文採訪老師及學生，了解他們在考察期間的所見所聞，以及對這類活動的看法。

articles.title: 前線報導：BBC走訪中尼邊境被洪災抹去的小鎮
articles.description: BBC記者阿扎德·莫希里來到夏布盧貝西，這裡緊鄰中國西藏吉隆，曾經生活在這裡的社區已幾乎不留任何痕跡，取而代之的是大量乾硬的泥土和瓦礫。

articles.title: 數百名水力發電工人受困隧道：尼泊爾地下夢魘
articles.description: 數百名工人的家屬仍抱持希望，相信受困於尼泊爾特里蘇里河（Trishuli River）沿岸龐大、充滿泥漿的隧道網絡中的親人仍有機會被活著找到。

articles.title: 星巴克咖啡就算了吧——Z世代喜歡喝冰飲
articles.description: 年輕消費者偏好冷飲和客製化飲品，到星巴克買熱咖啡不是他們的第一選擇。

articles.title: 美國NASA全新超強望遠鏡將改寫我們對宇宙的理解
articles.description: 羅曼太空望遠鏡（Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope）8月30日從佛羅里達州肯尼迪太空中心發射升空。

articles.title: 塔吉克斯坦年輕人之間緣何興起「漢語熱」？
articles.description: 直到幾年前，英語仍被塔吉克年輕人視為最重要的外語，但隨著中國在中亞地區的經濟影響力不斷擴大，漢語成為了對年輕一代更具吸引力的選擇。

articles.title: 她放下演藝事業，回愛丁堡拯救家裏的中餐館
articles.description: 母親經營了30年的餐廳正在走下坡。因此，賀灕灑暫停了自己的演藝事業，回到蘇格蘭的家裏試一把。

articles.title: 中國審查西藏口岸遭洪災衝擊畫面，當地災民情況我們所知甚少
articles.description: 一些關於這場致命山洪暴發最驚人的畫面，中國官方媒體未對公眾播放。

articles.title: 中國總理赴泥石流災場前線意味著什麼？
articles.description: 在中國，災難應對往往也帶有政治訊號。尤其是中共中央總書記作出「重要指示」，或總理、副總理親赴現場，通常意味著北京把事件視為需要高度關注和統籌應對的重大危機。

articles.title: 中國科技公司新嘗試：「性愛」機器人，瞄準「陪伴經濟」
articles.description: 近年來，中國的「陪伴經濟」異軍突起，AI和機器人技術的高速發展亦給這個市場注入諸多新的可能。

articles.title: 「在我眼中它就是黃金」：一張卡如何從遊戲工具變資產？
articles.description: 市場分析公司統計，全球集換式卡牌（TCG）市場規模到2031年有望升至128.6億美元。原本屬於小朋友的遊戲工具，何以突然變成「紙上黃金」？

articles.title: 這些藥物讓人更難以應對高溫
articles.description: 一些最常獲處方的藥物，包括用於治療抑鬱症、注意力不足過動症（ADHD）和高血壓的藥物，可能會增加脫水及其他與高溫相關疾病的風險。

articles.title: 「甲醛白菜」再現中國：食品安全監管的盲區在哪裡？
articles.description: 近日，中國河北省被揭發收購商為達到保鮮效果，將大白菜蘸取工業甲醛，再裝車運輸到外地，事件引發官方及輿論高度關注。

articles.title: 人形機器人以外，一場中國機器革命正靜悄悄地發生
articles.description: 中國工廠裡有超過兩百萬台機器人正在工作——而且它們的數量還在快速增長。

articles.title: 我六歲就來月經了，但醫生們也不知道為什麼
articles.description: 性早熟會導致兒童過早出現第二性徵，而且對女孩的影響比例明顯較高。

articles.title: 霍爾木茲海峽動盪，如何在巴拿馬運河引發中美角力？
articles.description: 美國和中國再次就巴拿馬運河問題交鋒。這條戰略水道約佔全球海運貿易量5%，而美國近40%的集裝箱運輸都經過這裏。

articles.title: 美國稱數十國助中國避特朗普關稅
articles.description: 美國一份新報告稱，中國透過關稅較低的國家轉運貨物，以規避較高關稅。

articles.title: 特習會後美中再現摩擦　「建設性穩定」能否撐到九月？
articles.description: 關稅、台灣、安全議題再起摩擦，特習會後的美中「建設性穩定」還能持續多久？

articles.title: 中美俄的太空攻防戰：衛星如何成為現代戰爭的第一擊？
articles.description: 在現代戰爭中，環繞地球運行的人造衛星幾乎未曾受到波及；但到了21世紀，太空或許已不再是安全的避風港。

articles.title: 特朗普政府禁止中國人形機械人進口 北京批「泛化國家安全」
articles.description: 美國和中國正陷入一場爭奪全球機械人與人工智能領導地位的競賽。
